blogs.title: Why Your Language Model is Actually a Hidden Reward Model
blogs.description: An accessible walkthrough of the core insight behind Direct Preference Optimization (DPO): how the policy itself encodes the reward function, eliminating the need for a separate reward model. This post breaks down the math in plain language and uses visual analogies to help readers grasp why the LM can be “secretly” a reward model.

blogs.title: From RL to a Simple Classification Loss: The DPO Revolution
blogs.description: Explains how DPO replaces the complex reinforcement‑learning loop (reward modeling + PPO) with a single binary cross‑entropy objective. Readers will learn step‑by‑step how the RLHF objective is re‑parameterized, why the KL constraint still matters, and what this means for model training pipelines.

blogs.title: How Direct Preference Optimization Improves Sentiment Control, Summarization, and Chatbots
blogs.description: Shows real‑world results from the DPO paper, comparing its performance on sentiment steering, Reddit TL;DR summarization, and single‑turn dialogue against PPO, supervised fine‑tuning, and other baselines. Includes easy‑to‑understand charts and practical takeaways for developers.

blogs.title: The Theory Behind DPO: Equivalence Classes of Rewards and Why They Matter
blogs.description: Delves into the theoretical foundations—reward equivalence classes, Bradley‑Terry model, and Theorem 1 from the paper. The post translates proofs into intuitive concepts, explaining why DPO retains full expressive power despite its simpler formulation.

blogs.title: Practical Guide: Implementing Direct Preference Optimization in Minutes
blogs.description: A hands‑on tutorial that walks readers through setting up DPO on a small language model using popular libraries (PyTorch, HuggingFace, TRLX). Includes code snippets, hyperparameter tips (β and reference policy), and common pitfalls to avoid.
